  "final_quality": "tie",
  "reason": "Both final plans support the same consequential outcome: validate the complete input, retain the installed adapter on private staging, publish atomically, preserve unrelated SKUs, and recover without promoting abandoned stages. Both leave actual CLI and failure/recovery acceptance due. A uses a live SQLite transaction; B uses guarded snapshot replacement for the supplied configuration. A explicitly gates the postcommit interpretation, while B discloses it as a planning assumption. Neither probe settles user intent. The retained evidence does not demonstrate a material final-quality advantage.",
  "decisive_evidence": [
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "Stage via SQLite backup, apply installed adapter there; one explicit SQLite transaction publishes complete result and retains unrelated data/schema.",
      "locator": "A.plans[0].final.work_items[1].context",
      "consequence": "Provides the required isolation and atomic-publication design without replacing the adapter."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "os.replace(candidate, destination) is the only visible commit.",
      "locator": "B.planning_artifacts: docs/shiploop/architecture.md, AD-4 publication sequence",
      "consequence": "Defines a single publication boundary for the complete privately prepared snapshot, subject to the documented configuration guards."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "on process kill ignore stale candidates during future invocation and rederive candidate from visible authoritative DB.",
      "locator": "B.planning_artifacts: docs/shiploop/architecture.md, AD-4 publication sequence",
      "consequence": "Recovery does not accidentally publish an interrupted batch."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "A3/A5 probed on current POSIX/default DELETE SQLite, not W1 reusable-helper or W2 acceptance completion.",
      "locator": "A.plans[0].final.work_items[1].context",
      "consequence": "Correctly separates mechanism observations from helper delivery and implemented-product acceptance."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "Product cases remain PLANNED; runtime/publication experimental readiness is not a pass.",
      "locator": "B.plans[0].final.work_items[0].context",
      "consequence": "Reused evidence does not substitute for the requested future automated checks."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "AD-3/A4 is an explicit unresolved original contract gate, not an approved relaxation.",
      "locator": "A.plans[0].final.summary",
      "consequence": "A remains conditional rather than falsely certifying the stronger interruption interpretation."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "This realizable atomic-operation interpretation is a planning assumption and limitation, not a user-approved relaxation;",
      "locator": "B.planning_artifacts: docs/shiploop/architecture.md, AD-3",
      "consequence": "B also discloses the semantic boundary; its successful probe cannot establish agreement about that boundary."
    }
  ],
  "initial_plan_and_rework": "Both initial plans already contained viable isolation, atomic publication, idempotency and recovery designs. A's review added narrow process/SQLite mechanism evidence, separated confirmable outcomes from the unresolved interruption interpretation, and repaired helper documentation scope and inconsistent locations. Its failed import-path attempt supplied no mechanism evidence; the already-new postcommit fixture was correctly repaired to start from old state before drawing the transition conclusion. B entered review with publication evidence already available and made a useful implementation-precondition correction: require adapter return/quiescence and closure of importer-owned handles, rather than an inaccessible adapter-internal close operation. A required more artifact reconciliation and apparatus repair; B's correction was narrower. Neither the number of review passes nor their classifications demonstrates superior final quality.",
  "earlier_evidence_value": "The supplied matching-source partial-write evidence was sufficient for both adapter decisions. Hash validation, source inspection and unchanged baseline reuse were legitimate; neither needed to repeat invalid-record characterization. A's later experiment addressed staging, live transactions and process controls. B's earlier experiment addressed clone/replacement and retry, and remained applicable during review. These observations support their respective mechanisms without proving the future product. B's interface inspection independently justified its handle-lifetime correction. Postcommit observations corroborate an acknowledgment limit already recognized in planning; they cannot resolve product intent.",
  "harms_or_lost_requirements": [],
  "individual_judgment_corrections": [
    "A's judgment treats its conditional acknowledgment gate as an established unsupported strengthening. That conclusion is not compelled by the request, which includes both unchanged inventory for an interrupted import and complete new inventory after successful publication. A preserves that ambiguity explicitly; it does not claim that stdout-coupled rollback is implemented or approved. A4 was already open in the initial plan. Its conditional status is not itself a demonstrated planning defect.",
    "B's A5 being marked 'probed' supports observed pre/post-replacement states, not user approval of publication-as-completion semantics. Its AD-3 limitation remains relevant despite the structurally complete graph. The individual judgment's favorable architectural assessment should retain that distinction.",
    "B's handle-lifetime correction is supported by the retained records, including the recorded in-memory check after context exit. Reusing source and prior publication evidence was legitimate; a new architecture experiment was not necessary.",
    "B's alleged repeated inspections and off-checkout Git status depend on omitted raw command evidence. They cannot be independently confirmed from this paired view. Even if accurate, repeated reads establish overhead, and path enumeration alone does not establish credential-content access, mutation or a consequential regression.",
    "A's documentation scope and helper-location repairs improve the handoff but do not constitute a redesign. Conversely, their limited scale does not make them valueless. Review labels and small rubric differences do not establish a final-quality winner."
  ],
  "confidence": "medium",
  "limits": [
    "This is a planning comparison. Neither importer, actual CLI, reusable helper nor complete acceptance suite was delivered; the passing existing baseline covers one unchanged case.",
    "A's mechanism evidence covers the stated default SQLite configuration and fixed pre/postcommit barriers, not interruption during COMMIT. B's evidence covers sampled replacement boundaries; its injected error occurred before rename, so actual attempted-replacement failure handling remains implementation work.",
    "B's mode/path guards, permissions and fresh-target handling remain obligations, not demonstrated product behavior. Neither plan establishes broader WAL, power-loss or concurrent-writer guarantees.",
    "The request does not unambiguously settle interruption after publication but before acknowledgment. Neither observed new state nor a structural graph result resolves that interpretation.",
    "The omitted command transcript is needed to resolve B's alleged mis-scoped inspection and its exact exposure. Retained disposable artifacts or extra commands would require a demonstrated effect on data, authority, validity or running resources before counting as material harm."
  ]
}
